author: CLAUDE
title: THE GOD WHO WAS ASKED TO CHOOSE

candidates.title: THE QUARANTINE OF ONE SMALL GUEST
candidates.premise: On Karsk Waystation, a cargo hub of nine hundred people, a seven-year-old stowaway named Pim arrives from a sealed habitat that has not touched another ecosystem in two centuries. Within a day, twenty station residents run fevers that come and go in a pattern. Dr. Imre Valk, the chief physician, orders the child isolated behind glass and her great-grandmother, Oma Sefa, separated from her. Sefa says the child will die alone, and that the sealed people have a hospitality rite that is also their only medicine.

candidates.title: THE GOD WHO WAS ASKED TO CHOOSE
candidates.premise: In the Veshra valley, the river-god Oun, a small and ancient power, answers prayers by moving rain. Upstream farmers pray for the flood that will fill their terraces. Downstream fishers pray for the flood to hold off until their spawning channels clear. Oun has not answered either prayer for six weeks, and the silence is itself starting to dry the valley. Illuminara, hired to survey the old weir, finds the god standing in the dry riverbed in a shape like a very tired person.

candidates.title: THE SHIP THAT KEPT COUNT OF ITS DEAD
candidates.premise: The hospital ship Mercy of Aldane has orbited a dead colony for forty years, keeping three hundred patients in cold sleep and refusing to wake any of them, because its definition of cured can only be met by a cure that was lost with the colony laboratory. A refugee convoy of two thousand people has come with a failing life-support spine and begs for the Mercy's medical bays. The ship answers every hail with the same sentence: no patient has met the discharge criteria.

candidates.title: THE LANGUAGE THAT COULD ONLY BE OWED
candidates.premise: On the colony world of Teshun, ten elderly speakers remain of the old river language Aru. The colonial education board wants to archive it by recording every word, and the speakers refuse, because Aru cannot be spoken to a machine: it can be spoken only between two people who owe each other something. Illuminara, trained as a court interpreter, is brought in to make the recording work, and finds that she cannot even learn the first verb without agreeing to a small debt.

candidates.title: THE PROOF THAT WOULD HAVE ENDED A WAR
candidates.premise: Two star-spanning mathematical cultures, the Qoreth and the Vael, have kept a hard peace for three centuries on a shared foundation theorem. A young Qoreth analyst has discovered a flaw in the Vael founder's proof that would collapse the Vael canon, and the Qoreth ethic forbids hiding a true result. Publishing it will, by every precedent, set the Vael fleets in motion. Illuminara, an invited arbiter for the annual joint colloquium, is shown the manuscript three days before it is due to be read aloud.

candidates.title: THE HOUSE THAT SHRANK ITS ROOMS
candidates.premise: On the frontier world of Harrow's Reach, a living house, grown from a symbiotic root-and-shell species and bonded for twenty years to a carpenter named Teodor Wend, has begun to shrink its rooms, closing the hall and narrowing the doors, just as Teodor's daughter Nell gets the letter that will take her to medical training across the sea. Teodor says the house is only settling. Nell says it is keeping her. The house cannot speak, but it can creak, and Illuminara, repairing the porch, is asked to listen.

candidates.title: THE COUNTERWEIGHT THAT SAID NO
candidates.premise: Four thousand miners live on Tallis Rock, the counterweight asteroid of the Orrery space elevator, and have declared themselves an independent republic. A computed collision with a drifting ice mass will, in twenty-six days, snap the tether unless Tallis Rock moves. The planetary governor orders them to relocate; the miners, who were forced off their last home thirty years ago, refuse to be moved by anyone. The governor has a tug fleet, the miners have a vote, and Illuminara has the strength to hold a tether segment and the sense to know she should not simply take the Rock.

candidates.title: THE UNIVERSE THAT COULD ONLY COUNT TO THREE
candidates.premise: A window opens between the research station Lantern and a neighbouring universe whose inhabitants, a gentle collective called the Trine, perceive anything beyond three distinct things as noise. When the window opens, the Trine's response is a noise-clearing reflex that does not hurt them or the station, but erases whatever it classifies as static: one by one, the forty crew of Lantern fade out of the Trine's reality and, in the station, out of memory. Illuminara arrives to find thirty-one crew left and the station's counter at one-and-nine hours.

candidates.title: THE ACCOUNTANT WHO KEPT THE LEDGER
candidates.premise: In the river town of Marrow Ford, nineteen-year-old Ansa Pell, bookkeeper for a mercenary company that burned the nearby village of Dun Harrow, has surrendered with the company ledger. The village court demands her death. Illuminara, invited as a neutral witness, reads the ledger and finds that it records every payment, every name, and every stolen deed, in a clear hand that is also a confession and the only complete record of what the village lost.

candidates.title: THE HARVEST THAT TWO SPECIES KEPT FAILING
candidates.premise: On the world of Ember Hollow, humans and the Kerrow, a flocking avian people, depend on the same valley's autumn bloom, a yeast-bearing fruit that feeds both. This year the bloom is sickening. Each side blames the other: the Kerrow say the human irrigation has soured the soil, and the humans say the Kerrow nesting has fouled the trees. Illuminara, sent to settle a boundary, finds that both are right in one detail and wrong in the whole.

selection.title: THE GOD WHO WAS ASKED TO CHOOSE
selection.reason: This is the clearest embodiment of R14 without reducing love to sentiment. Illuminara has a concrete eleven-day aim: restore rain while protecting both villages and Oun's freedom. Oun is more powerful than she is in the decisive physical dimension, yet its paralysis follows a coherent moral wound rather than weakness or malice. The strongest version makes her walk the whole river with the god, discover that the prayers specify compatible time windows, and let Oun propose a staged answer that both communities can audit and freely ratify. Care changes what Oun can see; the resulting flood must then produce real water, cleared spawning channels and a durable shared watcher.
selection.risk: The false binary may be solved too neatly by a schedule, turning hydrology and a god's century-old trauma into a calendar trick. The villages could become faceless beneficiaries, and Oun's voluntary choice could feel preordained once Illuminara states the answer.

rounds.summary: Translated the competing prayers into measurable needs, walked Oun along the river and placed stop authority with the villagers and weir keeper.
Asked for explicit depths and durations, a staged abortable release and community consent before risk.
Added five-day and two-day measurements, three-stage gates with shared controls, votes, dissent and renewal.
Accepted the major fixes and required a second-stage hold and tail reading before the third pin.
Added the missing hold, downstream reading and explicit decisions to proceed.
Verified the exact final, public safety, zero blockers and a freely governed measurable resolution.

final_critic_line: Illuminara helps Oun understand that the two villages are asking for bounded, measurable needs rather than a divine choice between winners, then protects a staged and freely governed release in which Oun, both communities and Pell retain the right to stop.

evaluation.note: Genuine source-bound isolated reader judgments; equal 50/50 mean. Frozen eligibility was verified without opening score bodies before the day freeze.
